# Human QA follow-up

Android 16, dark Chinese locale, 1220×2712 native capture; task-owned QA data.

- Settings/profile before images are the previously published `2648266f9c6bcb881f47383cb3eae69b67bc68c2` captures from the parent directory; after images show the new shared overlay tokens/frame. The usage aggregate increased as additional replay Bots were exercised; it is not a display change.
- Historical fade-only experiment images (not final pacing acceptance) are unretouched crops/contact sheets from native screen recordings, sampled at 30 fps over a 0.6-second window at source timestamp 5.0. Before (`f21`) is the rejected opacity-span experiment; after (`f22`) animates text-colour alpha. They replay the same `gentle` fixture at 3 graphemes/100ms through the real Host. Independent Host admission/commit latency means source text may advance on different sampled frames; compare the abrupt versus progressive appearance of the new glyphs, not latency or FPS.
- The complete private MP4s preserve original speed; contact sheets do not establish display frame rate. Public reproduction: `apps/mobile/scripts/stream-replay.md`.
- An earlier private `followup-visuals/before-settings.png` captured an unrelated foreground app and is invalid evidence. It is not published. `f17`/`f18` ran while Complete bubbles was selected and do not qualify streaming appearance. `f19` and `f21` opacity attempts did not establish a visible fade.
- The Human accepted the direction of reserved playback in f27, then requested speed/tail polishing and reported history dragging/jank. Final long-response naturalness, release frame-rate qualification, iOS native verification and keyboard speed remain outstanding.

`history-held.png` / `history-later.png` are native video frames at 14 and 17 seconds of `f34`, scaled to 488px width. They show the same historical paragraphs and jump control while all 21,492 characters commit behind the held cursor. The native row's anchor is unchanged even when Android compensates the removed working header. The original 32-second recording includes the drag, hold and explicit jump/resume. There is no comparable captured public Before for this newly reported gesture; the reported failure occurred during interactive QA, and static pre-existing images cannot establish pulling. Reproduction: select Streaming, receive the fixed `prose` fixture, drag toward older text while it grows, wait past Host commitment, then tap Jump to latest. The cursor must hold during reading and resume only on deliberate return.

The glyph-only f21/f22 comparison remains historical investigation, not proof that a network-chunk fade meets the accepted playback requirement. The final implementation uses a received-text reserve, independent cursor, rate-aware punctuation and retained draft/commit identity. Native recordings and bounded queue metadata are separate from FPS qualification.

`after-rich-playback.png` is the native f40 frame at 18 seconds, after the buffered 120-line code / 40-row table reply finishes. It is scaled to 488px width. The active 8–14-second window has 180/180 occupied frames and no nearly blank frames; that is a visibility check, not compositor FPS.
